g1-implement.title: G1 shared helper: implement scripts/work_id.py + tests/test_work_id.py
g1-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch constellation-implementer via run_crew.py. TASK: create C:/Programs/constellation-skills/scripts/work_id.py — the single work_id-safe parsing/matching helper both defect sites will import (this is what issue #716 asks for literally) — and C:/Programs/constellation-skills/tests/test_work_id.py. NOTHING ELSE: no call site is rewired in this gate and the installer is not touched, so the suite stays green (nothing imports the module yet). API, three functions, standard library only: (1) `work_id_from_session(session)` — invert `constellation/<work-id>/<gate>/<role>/attempt-<n>`. The last three segments are FIXED (gate and role can never contain '/': run_crew.run_log_paths uses them verbatim as filename stems), so for a name with >=5 segments work_id = '/'.join(parts[1:-3]). PER CRITIC FINDING F2 the back-compat fallback is NARROW: a name with FEWER than 5 segments cannot be the canonical grammar and reproduces today's parts[1] exactly; a >=5-segment name uses the right-anchored parse and NEVER guesses. A name whose first segment is not 'constellation', or with fewer than 2 segments, still raises (same refusal as today). State in the docstring which branch a given name takes. (2) `archive_dirs_for(archive_root, work_id)` — return the archive package directories for a work_id that may contain '/'. Rule: compare the path RELATIVE to archive_root; require the relative segment COUNT to equal the work_id's segment count; require all segments after the first to equal the work_id's segments after the first; require the first relative segment to equal the work_id's first segment OR to end with '-<first segment>'. For a 1-segment work_id this reduces EXACTLY to today's `name == work_id or name.endswith('-'+work_id)` — verify that equivalence with a test. PER CRITIC FINDING F3, ALSO match a FLATTENED single-level directory whose name equals or ends with '-' + the work_id with '/' replaced by '-' — this is load-bearing (someone may already have hand-flattened a package) and it is what makes the rejected naming-convention option cheap to adopt later. (3) `find_entry_heading(lines_or_text, work_id)` — pick the '## ' heading for a work_id. PER CRITIC FINDING F4 the rule is: prefer a heading containing an EXACT, delimiter-bounded occurrence of the work_id (the character before and after the match, where present, is not one of the work-id characters [A-Za-z0-9_/-]); ONLY if no such heading exists, fall back to today's plain substring behaviour. Do NOT use a longest-match rule — it returns the CHILD entry when a parent id is asked for, which inverts the bug being fixed. TESTS must cover, at minimum: a nested work_id round-trips through session_name -> work_id_from_session; a 3-segment work_id; the slashless case is byte-identical to today for all three functions; a <5-segment legacy session name; a non-'constellation' name still raises; the flattened-archive tolerance; a 1-segment work_id can NEVER match a 2-level package (segment-count guard); and the parent-vs-child heading case (asking for 'epic-659' when both '## ... epic-659' and '## ... epic-659/665' exist returns the PARENT). Wait for and integrate the returned IMPLEMENTER_RESULT.

triage_candidates.summary: recover_crews.py uses `import run_crew` (module-style), which the sibling-import guard's `^from (\w+) import` regex cannot see. It happens to be bundled wherever run_crew is, so nothing is broken today — but the guard is blind to that import form, which is the same class of silent distribution drift this run is fixing.

run_crew.py --verify-result reports 'result artifact absent' / an unrecognized-session refusal that names the session but never the parse, and load_registry treats a missing registry file as an empty registry — so a work-id resolution failure is indistinguishable from 'no crews yet'. Distinguishing them would have made issue #716 self-diagnosing on first contact.

No spine/skill template states that a work_id may contain '/'. init_work_area, stage_feedback and recover_crews all happen to be slash-safe via Path division, but that is incidental, not specified. A one-line contract in the schema doc would make the property intentional.

constellation-interrogator's SKILL.md tells the interrogator to `advance`/`skip` survey questions, but the engine refuses `advance` on a survey ('advance is for gated checklists; use record'). Doc-vs-engine drift, hit on every question of this run.
